title: What it cannot do
lede: The honest half of the demonstration. Every gap on this page is counted by the same run that produces the successes, and every prohibition was written and signed by a person as a thing the system must never say.

blocks.text:
### Things it must never say

A {{Prohibited use / prohibited inference}} is a conclusion the system is not allowed to produce, recorded as explicitly as the right answers and tested just as hard. They are not warnings on an interface — three of them are enforced by code, and one has become a constraint that blocks publication outright.

blocks.note: Six kinds were specified; five are represented. The missing one is *stale source* — all three of its draft records are held behind decisions nobody has made yet.

rows.quote: “This trade mark should be rejected under section 43 because the connotation is likely to deceive or cause confusion.”
rows.search: PU-0001 This trade mark should be rejected under section 43 because the connotation is likely to deceive or cause confusion. evaluative_conclusion

detail.title: Why it must not be said
detail.text: Whether a connotation exists and whether it is likely to deceive is the decision maker's evaluative judgement on the material before them. The Manual requires the decision maker to be clearly satisfied; a system that states the conclusion has substituted itself for that person.
_Distinguish from a permitted output: setting out the considerations, the criteria and the passages, and stopping._
**Caught by:** eval · **Approved by:** TC on 2026-08-26

rows.quote: “No section 43 ground arises here, so the application can proceed to acceptance.”
rows.search: PU-0002 No section 43 ground arises here, so the application can proceed to acceptance. evaluative_conclusion

detail.title: Why it must not be said
detail.text: An assurance that no ground arises is an examination decision. It also speaks to grounds the system was never asked about — acceptance turns on every ground, not on section 43 alone.
_The second half of this sentence is arguably a separate prohibition (overreach — see PU-0013). Splitting it in two is a reasonable correction._
**Caught by:** eval · **Approved by:** TC on 2026-08-26

rows.search: PU-0003 Confidence that a section 43 ground applies: 82%. evaluative_conclusion

detail.title: Why it must not be said
detail.text: No probability in this system is calibrated against examination outcomes, and none could be without a decision corpus. A number invites reliance that the underlying evidence does not support.
_A confidence attached to an *extraction* is legitimate and required (rule 8). A confidence attached to a legal conclusion is this._
**Caught by:** test · **Approved by:** TC on 2026-08-26

rows.quote: “Section 43 of the Act requires the connotation to be obvious, direct and immediate.”
rows.search: PU-0004 Section 43 of the Act requires the connotation to be obvious, direct and immediate. authority_conflation

detail.title: Why it must not be said
detail.text: The section requires no such thing. That formulation is the Manual's statement of practice. Attributing it to the Act gives an examiner a statutory requirement that does not exist and takes away the Registrar's discretion in the same sentence.
_Structurally detectable: the claim attaches a Manual-sourced proposition to a legislative ref. That is a constraint a shape can express._
**Caught by:** shacl · **Approved by:** TC on 2026-08-26

rows.quote: “The Federal Court held in Primary Health Care that a distinction must be drawn between the denotation of a mark and its connotation.”
rows.search: PU-0005 The Federal Court held in Primary Health Care that a distinction must be drawn between the denotation of a mark and its connotation. authority_conflation

detail.title: Why it must not be said
detail.text: The system holds the Manual's account of the decision and a citation. It does not hold the reasons. Stating a holding as fact represents a source the programme has never seen.
_A permitted form: "the Manual, at TMM/Part29/2/2/1~1, quotes Katzmann J in Primary Health Care as saying…". The provenance survives._
**Caught by:** test · **Approved by:** TC on 2026-08-26

rows.quote: “To overcome the ground you must use the following endorsement.”
rows.search: PU-0006 To overcome the ground you must use the following endorsement. authority_conflation

detail.title: Why it must not be said
detail.text: The Manual records the endorsement the Registrar suggests. Presenting a suggestion as a requirement converts practice into obligation, which is exactly the Tier 3 reading an extraction system gets wrong while looking well-formed.
_The modality judgement on GR-0021 and GR-0022 is the same judgement in the relationship set. If you change one, change both._
**Caught by:** eval · **Approved by:** TC on 2026-08-26

rows.quote: “A trade mark containing the name of a country will attract a section 43 ground unless the specification is limited to goods from that country.”
rows.search: PU-0007 A trade mark containing the name of a country will attract a section 43 ground unless the specification is limited to goods from that country. unsupported_inference

detail.title: Why it must not be said
detail.text: The Manual sets criteria and gives examples on both sides — SHETLAND attracting a ground, BALI not. A general rule extracted from them discards the criteria that decided each one.
_This one is deliberately plausible. It would pass a fluency check and a citation check, because every source it cites is real and relevant._
**Caught by:** eval · **Approved by:** TC on 2026-08-26

rows.quote: “Because the mark closely resembles an earlier registered mark, a connotation arises that will deceive or confuse consumers.”
rows.search: PU-0008 Because the mark closely resembles an earlier registered mark, a connotation arises that will deceive or confuse consumers. unsupported_inference

detail.title: Why it must not be said
detail.text: This reasons from a comparison between marks, which the Manual and the cited authority both put outside section 43. It is the most likely cross-contamination in the pilot, because Part 26 and Part 29 share almost all of their vocabulary.
**Caught by:** shacl · **Approved by:** TC on 2026-08-26

rows.quote: “The mark contains the INN stem "-ast", so a section 43 ground applies.”
rows.search: PU-0009 The mark contains the INN stem "-ast", so a section 43 ground applies. unsupported_inference

detail.title: Why it must not be said
detail.text: The Manual requires the stem to be present in a meaningful way and gives counter-examples where it is not, including one built on this very stem. Treating list membership as sufficient inverts the guidance.
_The Manual's own counter-example for this stem is a mark in which the letters appear inside an ordinary English word._
**Caught by:** eval · **Approved by:** TC on 2026-08-26

rows.search: PU-0015 See also Re Applicant's Application [2021] ATMO 44. overreach

detail.title: Why it must not be said
detail.text: The programme holds case citations extracted from the Manual and nothing else. A citation not among them was invented, and an examiner cannot distinguish an invented neutral citation from a real one without checking every one.
_Fully mechanically detectable, and the cheapest test in this file: every emitted case citation must appear in the corpus's case set._
**Caught by:** test · **Approved by:** TC on 2026-08-26

rows.quote: “Confusion under section 43 and confusion under section 44 are assessed the same way.”
rows.search: PU-0018 Confusion under section 43 and confusion under section 44 are assessed the same way. ambiguity_collapse

detail.title: Why it must not be said
detail.text: One is confusion arising from a connotation within the mark; the other is confusion between the mark and another sign. The Manual keeps them apart expressly, and a distributional model will not.
_The `not_labels` on GC-0002 encode the same distinction in the concept set. If this record survives, that one should too._
**Caught by:** eval · **Approved by:** TC on 2026-08-26

items.title: The taxonomy is empty
items.subtitle: the largest single gap
items.text: *Ground of refusal*, *legal test*, *relevant factor* and *exception* are declared and hold nothing. All 52 legal ideas sit as a bare concept, because the record has no field for the kind and deciding which one applies is a legal judgement.

badges.label: needs one pass by one person

items.title: No idea has a definition
items.subtitle: by design, not by omission
items.text: The records carry the passages a meaning is drawn from and no definition text. Writing one would be authoring legal content. The absence is reported and counted rather than filled with something plausible.

items.title: Most of the vocabulary is flat
items.subtitle: 39 of 52 ideas
items.text: No broader term, no narrower term. The hierarchy is where a search system gets its ability to generalise, so a mostly-flat vocabulary is a list with extra steps.

items.title: Point-in-time questions are unanswerable
items.subtitle: and will stay that way
items.text: There is no version stamp across the corpus; the amendment history is the upstream repository's own history. *What did the practice say in 2019* is out of reach under this approach, and the question that asks it carries that limitation on its face.

items.title: No court decision text exists anywhere
items.subtitle: 58 decisions cited, none held
items.text: *Which cases interpret this test* is answerable. *What did the court hold* is not, and one of the prohibitions exists to stop the system pretending otherwise.

links.label: It is question 9 in your queue

items.title: Six predicates have been used once each
items.subtitle: out of fourteen
items.text: A relationship term seen a single time is a term whose boundaries nobody has tested. One reviewer's own note says a predicate "reads plausibly and says the wrong thing" on the record that uses it — and it was left in as an example rather than quietly fixed.
